subject: Logic
title: Four Color Theorem
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Four Color Theorem.

hook.text: Any map can be colored with just four colors so no two neighboring regions share a color. Obvious? Try proving it.

buildup.text: Proposed in 1852, it resisted proof for over a century despite seeming obviously true.

discovery.text: In 1976, Appel and Haken proved it—but only by using a computer to check 1,936 configurations.

twist.text: Mathematicians objected: is a proof you can't verify by hand really a proof? The debate raged for years.

climax.text: It was the first major theorem proved by computer, forcing math to reconsider what counts as a proof.

punchline.text: Four colors suffice. A computer proved it.

quiz.question: Why was the four color theorem's proof controversial?
options: It required a computer to check cases, raising questions about proof standards
